stories.title: New Deputy Election Commissioner appointed in ECI amid concerns over work hierarchy
stories.summary: Prakash Rajpurohit fills the vacancy left by Sanjay Kumar’s premature repatriation, amid concerns raised by Election Commissioners S.S. Sandhu and Vivek Joshi over IT department files not being routed through him
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Prakash Rajpurohit, an IAS officer of the 2010 batch, has been appointed as a Deputy Election Commissioner in the Election Commission of India (ECI), filling the vacancy caused by the premature repatriation of Sanjay Kumar, who was incharge of the Electoral Rolls and IT division.

What will be the work allocation in the ECI after this new appointment is crucial, as Sanjay Kumar, who had been DEC from August 2024 till August this year, had been responsible for the electoral roll and IT divisions of the ECI, and had signed the ECI’s June 24, 2025, order initiating the SIR in the country.
It is also important because the two Election Commissioners S.S. Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had written to the Cabinet Secretary on how files of the ECI.
IT department head Dr. Seema Khanna not being routed through Mr. Kumar, who was a seasoned officer, was a violation.
Dr. Khanna joined the ECI in 2025 on deputation from the National Informatics Centre.
She heads the commission’s.
IT department, and oversees its digital infrastructure, including systems for electoral-roll management.

According to Election Commission sources, before the repatriation of Sanjay Kumar to his parent cadre, Dr. Khanna’s files had been routed through him till she was given a promotion to Level 15, which is equivalent to the rank of an Additional Secretary.

Since Mr. Kumar was of the rank of a Joint Secretary (which is Level 14), Senior Deputy Election Commissioner Manish Garg issued an internal order that Dr. Khanna’s files should go straight to the Election Commissioners from then.
This order was, however, never implemented.

Dr. Khanna’s files started being routed through to Maneesh Garg himself following the repatriation of Sanjay Kumar, as he was his link officer, which made him responsible for his departments in his absence.
Mr. Rajpurohit’s appointment was cleared by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet late on Saturday as per the order by the Department of Personnel and Training.

stories.headline: Waheed Para flags environmental risks in J&K’s 'Ease of Doing Business' bill
stories.title: Waheed Para flags environmental risks in J&K’s 'Ease of Doing Business' bill
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 11: Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) MLA Waheed Para has criticised the Jammu and Kashmir government’s new 'Ease of Doing Business' bill, alleging that the provisions could weaken land-use regulations, compromise urban planning and increase environmental risks in the region. In a post on X, Para reiterated his opposition to the legislation, arguing that provisions allowing commercial activities in residential areas and easing construction approvals could have serious implications for Kashmir’s fragile ecology and flood protection systems. Para shared a news report on the platform and questioned the extent of commercial development that could be permitted under the new framework, including concerns over the use of agricultural land for commercial structures. “Investment is welcome, but not at the cost of people's homes and safety,” Para said, arguing that planning regulations were essential to protect neighbourhoods and the environment. He claimed that shops and commercial establishments could operate in residential areas under the new provisions, with certain categories of industries and activities remaining excluded. Para also raised concerns over provisions that, according to his interpretation, allow residential buildings of up to 24 metres in height and 5,000 square metres to be constructed without conventional floor area ratio (FAR) or coverage limits, subject to certification by a government-approved consultant. He further questioned the approval requirements for malls of comparable size, arguing that the changes could reduce government oversight of large construction projects. Para linked the changes to Kashmir’s experience of the devastating September 2014 floods, warning that construction affecting drainage channels, wetlands and floodplains could aggravate future flooding. “We lived through the 2014 floods. We know what happens when drains choke and wetlands and floodplains are built over,” he said, adding that the provisions could put neighbourhoods, the environment and flood protection infrastructure at risk. Questioning the proposed reliance on consultant certification, Para asked who would ensure accountability and monitor compliance with construction norms. “A signed paper is not oversight,” he said, arguing that faster approvals should not come at the expense of regulatory safeguards. The PDP leader maintained that while investment was necessary for Jammu and Kashmir’s economic development, planning regulations were essential to protect residents and ensure sustainable growth.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Takes Note Of Fake Medical College In UP Operating From Farmhouse With Illiterate Tea Seller As Chairman
stories.title: Supreme Court Takes Note Of Fake Medical College In UP Operating From Farmhouse With Illiterate Tea Seller As Chairman
stories.summary: The Court directed the UGC and regulatory authorities to alert prospective students and members of the public to verify an institution's legitimacy before seeking admission or otherwise dealing with it.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Court directed the UGC and regulatory authorities to alert prospective students and members of the public to verify an institution's legitimacy before seeking admission or otherwise dealing with it.

The Supreme Court has taken note of a purported fake medical college in Uttar Pradesh allegedly operating from a dilapidated farmhouse, where an illiterate tea seller was shown as the institution's chairman and reportedly admitted to regularly signing documents provided by the person running it.

A Bench of Justice Ahsanuddin Amanullah and Justice N.V. Anjaria directed the University Grants Commission (UGC) and all regulatory authorities to issue public advisories cautioning people against taking admission to, or dealing with, educational institutions without first verifying their authenticity.
The Court also directed the Union Government to monitor compliance with the directions by the regulatory authorities.

“A suggestion has come from Mr. K.M. Nataraj, learned ASG, that the UGC, having come to know of such activity happening on the ground, may issue an advisory to all authorities/institutions, and especially to the public at large, not to take admission in or deal with institutions without first verifying the authenticity of such institutions.”, the Court said, after finding the suggestion to be useful and accordingly, a direction was issued to the UGC and all the regulatory authorities to issue such public advisory to act accordingly.
"We find the suggestion to be useful and accordingly, a direction is issued to the UGC and all the regulatory authorities to issue such public advisory to act accordingly.", the Court said.

The bench was continuing to hear a case concerning the functioning of educational institutions, including schools, colleges and universities in the country, after it was given a nationwide expansion, arising out of a matter relating to Amity University, Noida.
The Court took note of a newspaper report in The Indian Express concerning a purported fake medical college operating from a farmhouse in Mahmoodpur Nagaria village in Uttar Pradesh's Etah district.
According to the material placed before the Court, the institution purportedly offered courses including D.Pharma, B.Pharma, B.Sc.
Nursing, DMLT, BMLT, BAMS, GNM and ANM.

The Court observed that the institution appeared to be functioning from an old, dilapidated structure consisting of two or three rooms in the middle of a field, with no other structure visible nearby.
The building was also not properly maintained.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Acquits Man In POCSO Case Over Victim's Failure To Identify Him In Court, Unexplained Delay In FIR
stories.title: Supreme Court Acquits Man In POCSO Case Over Victim's Failure To Identify Him In Court, Unexplained Delay In FIR
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: A bench of Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta set aside the concurrent findings of the trial court and the Meghalaya High Court.
It found that the evidence of the victim's mother (informant), the victim and the victim's cousin was wavering and unreliable.

It is alleged that the appellant sexually assaulted the 40% intellectually disabled victim in 2015 when she was 11 years old, at her home when her mother (informant/PW 1) had gone out and she was alone.
PW 1 allegedly saw the accused plucking mulberry leaves in the garden next to the house as she left.
Thereafter, the victim then went to her cousin's house (PW 2) and stayed for the night.
The cousin told the victim's mother about the incident the next day, but the mother did not take it seriously because the child did not confirm the accusation.
Later, the victim disclosed the incident to her school teacher who informed the parents and an FIR was lodged nearly 10 days after the alleged incident.
The accused was then convicted by Special Judge (POCSO) and was sentenced to 10 years' rigorous imprisonment and a fine of Rs 1 Lakh.
The accused appealed before the High Court which dismissed his appeal in 2022.
Aggrieved by the High Court's dismissal, the appellant approached the Supreme Court.
Before the Supreme Court, Senior Advocate Gaurav Agrawal argued for the appellant (accused) that the prosecution had failed to explain the delay of nearly ten days in lodging the FIR.

It was submitted that PW 2 (victim's cousin) had told PW 1 (victim's mother/informant) about the incident on the very next day, yet this fact was not mentioned in the FIR, and the mother took no recourse to police action or medical assistance, which would have been the natural reaction had the allegations been true.

stories.headline: Jio-bp raises petrol price by ₹5 per litre, diesel up ₹3
stories.title: Jio-bp raises petrol price by ₹5 per litre, diesel up ₹3
stories.summary: While other fuel retailers have raised prices following the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, this is the first time Jio-bp has raised prices this year.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'petrol price' in title weight 40
article_sentences: Reliance Industries-backed Jio-bp has raised prices of petrol and diesel by ₹5 and ₹3 per litre, respectively, four people familiar with the development, including fuel pump dealers, said.
Following the increase, effective Sunday, petrol is being sold around ₹108.54 per litre and diesel at ₹99.19 a litre in Punjab, fuel retailers said.
In Haryana, Jio-bp pumps are selling petrol at around ₹109.80 per litre and diesel at ₹97.75 a litre.
Jio-bp is the second fuel retailer in the country to raise prices in the last 10 days.
Rosneft-backed Nayara Energy raised petrol and diesel prices by ₹5 and ₹3 per litre, respectively, on 3 October, as reported by the Press Trust of India.
Reliance and Nayara are also key exporters of petroleum products.
While other fuel retailers have raised prices following the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, this is the first time Jio-bp has raised prices this year.
Jio-bp imposed a cap of 50 litres per transaction on diesel sales in September.
"With this increase, the cap may become irrelevant as customers will move to other retailers," said a fuel retailer in Punjab on the condition of anonymity.

Neeraj Mittal, secretary to the Union ministry of petroleum and natural gas, had said on 1 October that the government would raise the recent diesel sales restrictions with private refiners and ask them to roll back the measures.
Jio-bp, which accounts for about a fifth of India's 99,400 privately operated fuel pumps, had earlier restricted diesel sales and imposed procurement quotas for its pumps in April.
State-run oil marketing companies (OMCs), which account for 90% of the country's fuel pumps, had also introduced rationing measures amid the West Asia war.

stories.headline: ‘India is moving forward with the dream of hosting 2036 Olympics’: PM Modi
stories.title: ‘India is moving forward with the dream of hosting 2036 Olympics’: PM Modi
stories.summary: Addressing the Golden Jubilee celebrations of Jaigopal Garodia Hindu Vidyalaya, PM Modi said hosting the world’s biggest sporting events in India would provide young athletes with a platform, better facilities and the support needed to pursue their ambitions.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Addressing the Golden Jubilee celebrations of Jaigopal Garodia Hindu Vidyalaya, PM Modi said hosting the world’s biggest sporting events in India would provide young athletes with a platform, better facilities and the support needed to pursue their ambitions.

Chennai: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday said India is moving forward with the dream of hosting the 2036 Olympic Games, expressing confidence that the country’s youth would take Indian sports to new heights as the nation prepares to host major international sporting events.
“India is preparing to host the 2030 Commonwealth Games.
We are also moving forward with the dream of hosting the 2036 Olympics,” PM Modi said.
“In the coming years, when the world’s biggest sports events will be held in India, the youth of India will have a platform, potential and support,” he added.
PM Modi said the opportunities for young people in sports were expanding as the country developed new facilities and strengthened training and support systems for athletes.
“Every youngster has their own unique dreams and talents.
For example, I am sure there are many of you who want to make sports their career.
This is why the country is ensuring that sports should not be limited to entertainment only,” he said.
PM Modi said young players were receiving better training and support, while India’s position in international sports was also improving.
“It means the opportunities are endless.
I am confident that your generation will take India to new heights in the world of sports,” PM Modi said.
